cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ, is writing to the church in Corinth, and he's been defending his work against some who commend themselves (2 Corinthians 10:12). Now he asks them for a little patience: “I hope you will put up with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.” Friend, that's like asking somebody to sit through your vacation photos when they're already on slide FORTY!
Then Paul says he's jealous for them, with a godly jealousy. He paints a wedding picture: he promised them to one husband, and he wants to present them pure.

cards.question: In Paul's wedding picture, he promised the Corinthians to one husband. Who is the husband?

cards.text: But Paul is worried. He reaches all the way back to the garden, to someone who got deceived by the serpent (Genesis 3:13).

cards.question: Paul writes to the Corinthians that ___ was deceived by the serpent's cunning.
Paul is afraid that the Corinthians' minds could be led astray from their simple and pure devotion to Christ, just as Eve was deceived.

cards.text: Paul spells out the danger: someone proclaiming a Jesus other than the One Paul proclaimed, or a different spirit, or a different gospel. Friend, that's not a new flavor, that's a whole different cookie wearing the old label!

cards.question: If someone comes preaching a different Jesus or a different gospel, how does Paul say the Corinthians handle it?

answers.text: They put up with it very easily
They send the preacher away fast
They argue about it for days

cards.text: Then Paul brings up a group he calls those “super-apostles.” I don't know about you, friend, but I'm picturing CAPES.

cards.question: How does Paul say he measures up next to those super-apostles?

cards.text: Paul admits he's not a polished speaker. Hey, ME NEITHER, friend, my greatest speech ever was to a scared can opener in the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: Paul says that besides not being a polished speaker, he's lacking in knowledge too.

cards.text: Then Paul asks the Corinthians a question, and I hear a little edge in it. Was it a sin for him to humble himself so he could lift them up?

cards.question: Paul asks if it was a sin for him to humble himself in order to lift up the Corinthians. What had he done for them?

answers.text: Preached the gospel free of charge
Refused to stay in anyone's home

cards.text: Paul says he “robbed other churches” by accepting their support so he could serve the Corinthians. Friend, that's like letting one buddy pay for your gas so you can drive another buddy to the airport for FREE!

cards.question: When Paul was with the Corinthians and in need, the Corinthians supplied what he needed.

cards.text: When Paul was in need there, the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied his needs. He wasn't a burden to anyone.

cards.question: Paul hasn't leaned on the Corinthians in any way. What does he say he'll do from now on?

cards.text: Paul says, as surely as the truth of Christ is in him, this boasting of his won't be silenced in Achaia, the region where Corinth sits. Then he asks, “Why? Because I do not love you?” and friend, I bet there's some hurt behind that one.

cards.question: Paul answers his own question by saying God knows he loves the Corinthians.

cards.text: Paul isn't changing a thing: he'll keep on doing what he's doing. Friend, that's me every time somebody says the mustache could use a trim!

cards.question: Why will Paul keep preaching to the Corinthians free of charge?

answers.text: To undercut men who want to seem his equals
To win over the leaders in Jerusalem
To set an example for the Macedonians

cards.question: Paul gives a name to the men who want to be seen as his equals. He calls them ___ apostles.

cards.text: Paul says these men are masquerading as apostles of Christ. And no wonder, he says, because someone else wears a disguise like that too.

cards.question: Who does Paul say masquerades as an angel of light?

cards.text: So Paul says it's not surprising if Satan's servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Friend, I met a REAL angel once, in a junk drawer in the dark, and let me tell you, the real thing never needs a costume.

cards.question: Paul says these false apostles will get away with what they're doing in the end.
